DNK35895 is a specific laboratory code used within the Danish healthcare system to register the measurement of thyrotropin, commonly known as thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) [^src1]. In the context of national clinical quality monitoring, this code plays a precise administrative and clinical role. According to the "Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark" guidelines published by the Regional Clinical Qualityity Development Programme (RKKP), DNK35895 is one of the approved laboratory codes used to verify that a patient has undergone a TSH measurement [^src1]. 

This verification is a critical component of "indicator 3," a clinical quality metric designed to ensure that patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation receive appropriate diagnostic workups, including thyroid function testing [^src1]. When healthcare providers register a TSH test using DNK35895—or a set of other recognized NPU and ASS codes—it successfully counts toward the fulfillment of this quality indicator on page 105 of the RKKP documentation [^src1]. Ultimately, the code serves as a standardized data point linking clinical laboratory practice to the broader national quality assurance frameworks for [[thyreoideastimulerende-hormon-tsh|thyreoideastimulerende hormon (TSH)]] monitoring in atrial fibrillation patients [^src1].
